Lately I've discovered I really like getting up at around 3am and writing for about 4-5 hours in the morning. I'm not a morning person, but I am an insomniac. I've always liked the wee hours. I'm not sure if it's the stillness of the morning, the mental emptiness from sleep or the quiet or what. My writing productivity drops substantially after about 11am. I pretty much can't write creatively in the afternoon or the evening. But that's ok, because I typically have classes in the afternoon and I work in the evening. So a morning for writing seems to fit well with me, because I can take a nap before class.

What about the rest of y'all? Is there a time of day you write better?

Books and comics books are my preferred medium, since when a book gets adapted into a movie I nearly always prefer the book. Comic books are perfect for telling stories that rely on action and imagery. You can do things with words and text that don't survive the transition to another medium, like suddenly change the art style, for example.

I don't think anything compares to a a good story told in person. It's a bit of a lost art, but I love those moments when someone keeps me and a small group of people enchanted with some story they tell. There is something very primal about it, and why I think people that can tell a good story tend to be very popular.
The written word, but as noted a storyteller can be captivating.

Books, but I really wish the game developers would get their shit together and develop a decent non-linear narrative structure. I've been waiting twenty years for it and they are all still basically screwing around with the graphics. With VR coming down the pipeline I don't expect them to switch gears anytime soon.

Friendships are made based on circumstances and or mutual interests. Childhood friendships seem to be the strongest, but they don't necessarily have to exist day to day for them to last a lifetime.

It seems to me that friendships are strongest and longest lasting when you have gone through adversity together. For friendships to last on a regular basis, there must be a strong mutual interest.

Friendships are few, and that is because so much time and energy must be invested in one. This does not have to be a hardship, but time and energy is necessary.

I believe most people have more aquaintences than friends in a lifetime. This may have more to do with changing interests, lifestyles, and responsibilities. It is also why anyone who has one, maybe two, friends is truly lucky. Not everyone we know is worth the time and energy needed to sustain a friendship.

Find people you enjoy being around and be around them when you can. At the very least find people you enjoy doing specific things with and try to schedule a routine.

If you can't find people you enjoy being around, there's something you need to work on or keep looking. If you have any hobbies, that can be a good form of casual bonding.
